one_month_reasoning: The 1m window ends at the Oct 30 close (Nov 1 is a Sunday). I now think Booking's Q3 print is most likely just outside it: Booking gives ~4 weeks' notice (Sep 30, 2025 for the Oct 28, 2025 print; Jul 7 for the Aug 4, 2026 print) and EDGAR shows no 8-K since Aug 4 as of Oct 2 [18][20]; aggregators estimate ~Nov 3. I put ~15% on a print inside the window. Expedia and Airbnb Q3 reports are also usually early November, so the industry read-through I leaned on in round 1 mostly lands after the window. Inside the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC (after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%), Middle East/oil headlines, and AI-agent news (Meta Muse/Google) that moved the group 5%+ in single days in September [8][20]. Ladder: 85% a no-print lognormal with ~10% monthly sigma (38%/3.5 ~ 11%, slightly narrowed) and modestly fat tails, 15% an earnings-widened ~15% sigma; median ~$159.6, i.e. essentially at spot with only a token reversal tilt after the -20% August-September slide. I removed the round-1 beat tilt.

bear.story: AI agents (Meta Muse with Expedia, Google, ChatGPT) visibly divert demand and force take-rate concessions; Airbnb keeps taking alternative-accommodation share; Middle East/oil and a hiking Fed hurt long-haul; FTC complaint and EU parity damages add overhang. ~$11 EPS x ~10x.

base.story: Bookings grow mid-to-high single digits in line with Expedia, low-to-mid-teens EPS growth from buybacks and transformation savings; Middle East drag fades; AI stays a multiple overhang but Booking participates as a supply/merchant partner. ~$13.25 NTM EPS x ~14x minus some residual discount.

bull.story: Long-haul recovery, Booking signs visible AI-agent distribution deals, fears ease and the multiple re-rates to ~17x on ~$14 NTM EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$118 the stock would be ~9.8x my 2027E EPS of $12.05 and ~25% below the Sep 23 closing low ($155.90); that most likely reflects a fundamental break rather than volatility: room nights flat/negative while Expedia and Airbnb grow, evidence of take-rate compression from AI-agent channels, or an EPS guide-down to single-digit growth. The 52-week low ($150.14 intraday, May 20) shows ordinary sentiment shocks have held above ~$150.

reasoning: Round 2 changes: (1) Facts corrected per supervisor: shares outstanding 751.4M at Jul 27 (verified on the 10-Q cover [17]), market cap ~$120B; consensus FY26 $10.45 / FY27 ~$12.37 (Sep 24) [19]; the Q3 print is likely ~Nov 3 because no 4-week notice exists (EDGAR shows no 8-K since Aug 4 [18]). (2) As asked, I quantified the share-loss read like-for-like on Q3 guides: BKNG gross bookings +4-6% (+5-7% CC, ~1pt FX headwind) and room nights +3-5% [1]; Expedia gross bookings +5-7% with FY raised to +8-9% [3]; Airbnb GBV mid-teens incl ~3pt FX tailwind with nights low double digits [4]. So against Expedia Booking trails by only ~0-1pt, and the real share loss is to Airbnb in alternative accommodation (BKNG alt-accom nights +4% in Q2). My round-1 framing overstated it; I cut the FY27 haircut from 3.5% to 2.5% ($12.05). (3) Multiple: FY27 consensus held through the September sell-off, so the ~20% drop is mostly multiple; holding 13.5x flat was a little punitive and I move to 14x (not the 15-18x historical range, since Muse/Expedia and Google are a structural rather than cyclical threat). Fair value ~$188 (P/E $185, FCF $194), up from $182. Scenarios $110/$183/$238 at 25/50/25 give mean ~$179 and median ~$174. The 12m ladder is a lognormal-mixture centred at ~$174 (80% at 31% vol, 20% at 50% vol for AI/legal tail risk), so the effective spread is ~35%, slightly under the realized 38-39%. The 1m ladder is now near-symmetric around spot because the print is probably outside the window. Industry demand context is unchanged: Marriott and Hilton guide RevPAR +3-3.5% with Middle East weakness [5][6], Trip.com outbound hotel +5% [7]. Research in round 2 was limited to primary SEC documents; StockAnalysis did not render, so the consensus figure relies on the supervisor's check.
